prospect.name: Nader
prospect.location: Utah, USA — moved there two days before the call
prospect.occupation: Resident doctor in radiology, in the final year of a five-year residency. Works close to 80 hours a week and describes the job as entirely sedentary — 'my job is radiology. So I read imaging for people.'
prospect.family_status: No children; wants them in future
prospect.training_background: Peak condition in college, graduating 2016 — around 170-180 lb, deadlifting 365 lb for five reps and benching 185-200. Nothing consistent in the ten to twelve years since, through medical school and five years of residency. Has gained roughly 80 lb over that period. Played football for many years as a striker and can no longer manage it without knee pain. Currently does no structured training.
prospect.medical: Occasional mid to low back pain, worse depending on how he slept, which he attributes to being hunched at a desk and to the weight gain. Occasional neck pain. Knee pain when he plays football, though not in daily life. Cardiovascular fitness self-rated 2 out of 10, with shortness of breath climbing three flights of stairs. Poor sleep quality, raised by him as something he wants to fix. No conditions, medications or clinician involvement disclosed, and none were asked about. Weight is recorded as 255 lb, the midpoint of his own '250, 260 pounds'.

signals: Lost ground to a defined hard season and can date it precisely: 'I graduated college in 2016, so it's been 10 years... four years of medical school... five years of residency... And I am tired of being like this.'

Wants a specific former self back, with the physical evidence kept: 'I even have clothes that I had from college. I'm just like, I really don't want to get rid of this because one day I want to lose weight and wear this again.'

Visible regret, stated plainly: 'I look at pictures of myself before, used to be like very lean, healthy. Now I do not feel like that. It just bothers me. I'm like, I'm only 32 years old. So I should be in my peak physical.'

The ambition has recalibrated from aesthetics to function — 'it used to be like a bodybuilding physique in college... but now it's more functional, like I want more functional strength that I don't want my back to be hurting'

goals.text: Lose a large amount of body fat while preserving muscle — 'if you lose weight and half of it's muscle mass, what's the point?'
Get to roughly 10% body fat and see abs, from a self-estimated 30%
Get under 200 lb within six to twelve months, from 250-260
Functional strength rather than size — 'I don't want to look like Ronnie Coleman'; Trevor's physique is the reference
Cardiovascular capacity — not be short of breath on three flights of stairs
Get rid of the back and neck pain
Fit back into the clothes he has kept from college
Be healthy and capable before he has children — 'if you want to be a dad and your kid wants to go kick football and you can't even do it because you're out of breath'
Longevity and overall health, stated as a doctor's judgement about his own trajectory

pains.text: Roughly 80 lb gained over ten to twelve years of medical training

An 80-hour working week, previously with a two-hour daily commute on top — 'when I come home, it's more like I need to take a shower, need to go to the bathroom, need to make some food, need to sleep'
Entirely sedentary work reading imaging at a desk
Cardiovascular capacity self-rated 2 out of 10, short of breath on three flights of stairs
Occasional mid to low back and neck pain, which he links to the desk and the weight
Cannot play football at the level he used to without knee pain afterwards
Finds treadmill cardio intolerable — 'doing cardio all day long just on a treadmill is torture, to be honest'
No idea how to use a kettlebell safely — 'I would just be picking it up and swinging it all over the place'
Ten years of being unhappy about it and unable to act — 'for so many years I've been wanting to, but I can't because I'm just so restricted with the time'

objections.raw_quote: That's steeper than I thought you were going to say, to be honest... I'll be honest with you. If I had known that it was that much, I probably wouldn't have wasted your time. I can't, that's like impossible... It's not even, even if you said three, it's impossible. I can't. It's literally, literally impossible.
objections.rep_response: Isolated properly and twice — 'let's say, out of the blue, six grand would fall on your lap, would you be like, okay, Richard, let's just go?' and 'do you feel like yes is actually something you see yourself doing outside of the financial aspects?' — then asked what amount would have been possible, then suggested a credit card and third-party financing. Both were refused. Then offered the $200/month tier.

objections.raw_quote: something like this would not be even feasible for me for another earliest, earliest, like the best case scenario, this is a year from now. Like, it's not even possible... maybe 16 months, maybe it's possible. Maybe. Now it's like, there's no chance. You have a better chance of, like, me getting hit by lightning.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it and pivoted to staying in touch — 'if it's not now, it's something for in the future, but at least we have an idea from what we're working with' — then offered Primal University and promised to send materials.

objections.raw_quote: I would have preferred if you guys at least had something on the website talking about the rate, because maybe you feel like your time wasn't wasted, and it was a nice conversation, but I now, I did lose an hour, because this, if I had known the cost, I would have never, ever set the meeting up, taken somebody's spot.
objections.rep_response: [proposed type: price_transparency_complaint] Did not engage with the substance. Answered by offering the $200/month tier and promising to send some materials so he was not left empty-handed.

objections.raw_quote: I haven't done this before for me to be like, I did this and it worked and I know it works. I don't have an anecdotal history of it. Anecdotally, I have had success counting my calories, lifting weights, running or doing cardio the traditional way. So I know that works. So I'm not going to lie to you and be like, yeah, I think this will definitely work. I'm hoping it works.
objections.rep_response: Answered with scale as proof — 'Trevor coached more than 1,200 people' and 'he has 1.3 million followers on Instagram, it would probably be all over the place, right, if it wouldn't work' — which the prospect accepted as fair. He then rated the programme 8.5 out of 10.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No instalment plan was offered. Two funding methods were floated after the refusal and both were declined outright: 'a lot of people, of course, they don't have the financials all in one place, so they sometimes decide to put on a credit card in America. I'm just curious, is that something you would be able to do?' answered 'No, no chance. I'm not going to ruin my credit, man', and third-party financing answered 'I'm not going to take out a loan, no... I could be Jeff Bezos, and I would never do that.'

prospect_financials.note: No figures were gathered; everything here is his own framing. He expected 'maybe it was like a couple hundred dollars. The high end, maybe it's like sub a thousand', described $6,000 and $3,000 as literally impossible, ruled out credit cards and loans on principle, and put the earliest feasible date at twelve to sixteen months away.

evidence: Explicit and repeated refusal of the offer: 'that is impossible for me to do. Like, that's not even remotely possible' and 'Even if you told me it was three, I wouldn't be able to do it'
Both funding routes refused on principle — no credit card, no loan
The prospect closed by saying the call itself had been a waste: 'I feel like I wasted your time, I feel like I wasted my time now'
Counter-evidence keeping a thread open: he answered 'Okay, I'll think about it' to the $200/month Primal University tier, and the rep committed to sending materials

Counter-evidence on intent rather than outcome: he rated the programme 8.5 out of 10 before the price and said 'I would be willing to try and start first workout tomorrow'. This was lost on price alone, not on fit or belief.
outcome.next_step: Rep to send free materials and information on Primal University at $200/month; prospect to consider it. No follow-up call was booked and no timeline was agreed.

notable.note: The most valuable ICP data point in the batch. The stated ICP names physicians explicitly, and this is the only actual physician in twelve files — and he is the furthest outside the ICP on every other criterion, having gained 80 lb across a decade of medical training and now sitting at roughly 30% body fat and short of breath on three flights of stairs. He is also the only prospect in the batch to reject the price outright rather than negotiate it, and he did so as a resident doctor: 'a couple hundred dollars. The high end, maybe it's like sub a thousand.' His closing complaint is the most actionable thing in this file — that no price appears anywhere before an hour-long call — and it lands directly against the position the sales manager stated a week earlier, that it does not matter if prospects arrive with the wrong price in their heads. He also refused both credit routes on principle after they were suggested, which is the fourth call in this batch where consumer credit was raised as the funding mechanism.

quality.notes: Sustained inversion throughout. Whole biographical passages sit under the rep's label — 'After college, I went to medical school, which took a lot of time to study' at 00:02:24 and 'And how old are you at the moment?' answered inside the same block at 00:04:46 — and the rep's questions repeatedly appear under the prospect. The long block at 00:06:00 attributed to the prospect is almost entirely the rep speaking. Role was read from content throughout, which is unambiguous here because only one participant is describing a medical residency and an 80-hour week. The prospect's surname is never spoken. The rep mishears or the transcript mangles 'why' as 'wife' at 00:15:34 and Trevor's name as 'Travis' at 00:48:54.
